title: Composable Papyrus plugins for GraphQL APIs and their frontend components
description: Goal: As a publication operator, I want Papyrus to compose enabled plugins during the normal build so one configured Amplify application and deployment includes new GraphQL API resources and the components that use their shared client/types. Ryan explicitly requested this initiative in the Papyrus product project. Present state: Amplify Gen 2, existing signup deploy-time plugin (PR #201 / a85ddb2), static Markus HTML published to S3, restricted editorial CMS. Foundation scope: validate enabled configuration/dependencies/collisions, deterministic native TypeScript schema/resource composition and frontend registrations, multiple resources/components per plugin, no-plugin parity, proof plugin and authorization/build tests. Prospectus later literally reuses Kanbus for CRM; private prospects remain separate from public lead submission. Excluded: full CRM, index invalidation, production migration, deletion, merge/deployment, persistent permission provisioning. Plan: inspect current mechanisms and Right Now, specify behaviors, implement in isolated worktree, independent review, checks, commit/push and draft PR; retain open status until landing.

comments.author: home
comments.text: CANCELED by Ryan on 2026-10-13: "take back that initiative about creating plugins into Papyrus, cuz I think we just eliminated that entire problem". Prospectus can use existing Kanbus/Virtuus issue storage as a separate application/subdomain with simple configured links/intake; the proposed plugin foundation is therefore no longer needed. All implementation agents stopped immediately. This is cancellation, not completed delivery. Partial work is preserved in the isolated feature/PPY-f8bbd3-plugin-build-foundation worktree and a local archive; no implementation was merged or deployed. No alternative CRM or baseline tables are being implemented. Supersedes this issue and its initiative plan.

right_now_summary: Ryan canceled the plugin foundation; no implementation was merged or deployed.
